pairs.why: A hangs flat on the wall like the real card, while B's round clock stands on its bare rim on the floor with no stand or foot to keep it upright.
A's keypad has no equals key because a wide 0 takes its place, so it couldn't work as a calculator; B has a complete 0 . = + bottom row.
B has four wheels on axles, small ones at the front by the tongue, but A's single shaft juts out of the side of the box behind the wheel, where nothing could pull it.

A's X-legs, seat and armrests connect into a frame that could fold and stand, but B's front seat bar sticks out past the legs and its back posts run into the X-legs in a way no real folding chair is built.
A's lifebuoy hangs from a post by a rope loop and the deck sits on its piles, while B's buoy is wedged over a short post in mid-deck with a rope sagging across it to the coil.
B hangs on the wall like the real card, while A's round clock balances on its rim on the floor with nothing to hold it up.
Both are a believable pedestal table with stools on the grass, and neither the boards nor the bases have a clear construction error that separates them.
A has a bench bolted to the side of the box and a tongue hanging off the side panel down to a T-bar on the ground, but B's four wheels and front tongue make a wagon that could actually be pulled.
